segments.text:
Date: 26-02-2019 and 13-06-2019

Case Number: 930 26022019

Report: An observation of a phenomenon filmed from Casablanca, Valparaíso Region, on Monday, 25 February 2019, around 20:30 (HL).

Description: The observer described it as having the shape of a "disc with lights."

Location: Casablanca

Region: Valparaíso

Classification: Resolved.

It described a cigar-shaped object, approximately 100 meters in size, located 10,000 meters away.

It stated that it had a reddish coloration and fixed direction of motion. It added that its initial impression was that it was a meteorite, which it dismissed due to the speed of the phenomenon. It also ruled out that it was an airplane, as it did not leave a white trail in its wake, but rather a trail attached to its body.

It was of a reddish color. He indicated that what was filmed was lost in the direction of sunset,
that its complete viewing lasted approximately 10 minutes, and that the same
aerial phenomenon would have been seen from the port of San Antonio, V region.

The recording was examined and it was determined that it corresponds to 12:14 minutes
filmed at 30 fps and that it shows no evidence of manipulation.

It was verified that for the city of Casablanca, sunset occurred at 20:26 (HL) and civil twilight ended at 20:51 (HL). This was consistent with the lighting conditions that made the aerial phenomenon filmed shine and the short condensation trail it generated.

Air traffic in the Casablanca area was investigated, finding that it was seen during the investigation.

A flight from the city operated by a institutional flight from Viña del Mar Airport (SCVM) (Figure 1). In turn, from San Antonio, the passage of JetSmart Airlines flight JAT237 was visible, heading from Andrés Sabella Airport in Antofagasta (SCFA) to Carriel Sur Airport in Concepción (SCIE). It was an A320 with registration CC-AWB, flying at 37,000 feet and 412 knots. (Figure 2)

Information was requested regarding a flight identified as possibly institutional with the Chilean Navy and the Viña del Mar Aerodrome.

Figure 1. Flight filmed

Figure 2. Flight possibly perceived from San Antonio

The study of the case background allowed concluding that what was reported near Casablanca was the air traffic of an institutional aircraft.

Conclusion: Additionally, it was determined that there was a commercial flight in transit from North to South, which could be seen from the port of San Antonio, corresponding to what the user reported.
